name: Badge
purpose: A short, non-interactive status label such as Paid, Overdue or Draft. Not a button, not a counter.
description: Status labels for records and rows. Six tones map to the status colour tokens; three variants trade emphasis for density. The text carries the meaning so colour is never the only signal.

tone.description: Meaning. success for settled or active, warning for pending or attention, critical for failed or overdue, info for informational, accent for highlighted, neutral for draft or archived.

variant.description: Emphasis. soft (tinted) is the default in tables; solid for a single prominent status on a detail page; outline for the quietest option.

size.description: 20 or 24 px tall. sm inside dense table rows.

dot.description: Leading dot in the tone colour, for live or state indicators.
dot.a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden). The text must still say the state.

a11y.name: The text content. A badge has no role; it reads as part of the surrounding text.
notes: Every tone pairing meets 4.5:1 for text in both themes.
Colour reinforces the word; it never replaces it. "Overdue" in critical, not a red dot alone.
Badges are not interactive. For a filter chip or a removable tag, a different component is needed (not in the system yet).

rules: The label is a word or two that states the status in plain language.
Tone follows meaning, not decoration: critical means failed or overdue, never "important".
One badge per status; do not stack badges to combine meanings.
dos: Use soft badges in tables and solid on a record's header.
Use dot with neutral for "Draft" and with success for "Active".
donts: Do not make badges clickable; they have no role and no focus style.
Do not use badges as counters; a count is Text numeric.
